A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Next-Gen CAPTCHAs framework and benchmark. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison; v1 Appendix B is retained as v2 Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original human and agent evaluations, trajectory analyses, and thinking-mode and framework ablations in Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–4 and 7–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a non-CS human evaluation, hint-assisted attack results, and measurements of dynamic-family asset payloads.

M1.justification: The CAPTCHA families, procedural generation, verification mechanisms and interaction framework are unchanged. The new hint-assisted attacker is an evaluation variant, while bandwidth-aware deployment options are recommendations rather than an implemented defense revision.

E1.justification: The 27 families and 519/135-puzzle benchmark sets remain unchanged. However, Appendix B adds a non-CS participant population, and Appendix C introduces attackers supplied with strategies derived from implementation code, substantially broadening the populations and attack conditions evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds a family-aware, hint-assisted Gemini-3-Flash-High/Browser-Use attacker alongside an unhinted baseline. The six main model backbones and the Browser-Use, CrewAI and Claude Cowork framework comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Existing main evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added protocols cover eight non-CS participants attempting one instance per family, baseline-versus-hint attacks with one strategy hint per family on 519 puzzles, and average visual payload measurement under cold loading.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a substantive robustness test against implementation-informed strategy hints across all families, exposing complete Red Dot success under adaptation. Appendix D adds analysis of deployment bandwidth burdens; the existing framework, thinking-budget and trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: There are no additions to repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty estimation. Figure 4 retains its correlation significance markers; the new participant-level accuracies are additional outcomes rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds 85.2% non-CS human success, family-specific human completion times, hinted attack success of 6.4% versus 3.2% baseline, Red Dot success of 100% versus 15%, and payloads of 0.47–9.23 MiB. Main results remain unchanged. Table 5's baseline differs inexplicably from Table 2 on several families, including Box Folding at 10% versus 0%; these are newly reported comparisons, not established same-setting revisions.

T1.justification: The extended POMDP definition, workspace updates, observation specification and cognitive-gap formulation in Section 4 and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about 27 human-friendly, agent-defensive families, scalable generation and a real-web evaluation platform. The conclusion receives wording edits without changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C interprets low aggregate hinted success as robustness while identifying gains concentrated in Red Dot. Appendix D adds deployment tradeoffs involving connection quality, device capability, caching and lighter task families. Existing cognitive-bottleneck and accessibility discussions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents the original human evaluation's CS background, 268 trials and absence of an explicit time limit. v2 also describes the hint-generation model and source inputs, participant attributes, and cold-load measurement definition. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to titles, authors, dates and publication metadata concern existing references; for example, the renamed Huang et al. and COGNITION entries retain their respective arXiv identifiers.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, adds acknowledgements and conference publication text, and inserts Appendices B–D before the retained family documentation. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Three appendix tables are added for participant characteristics, hint adaptation and payload measurements. The original family catalog becomes Table 7, and gallery figures are redistributed across pages. Existing figures and main table displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central usability and security claims more assessable by documenting the original human study and adding non-CS users, informed attackers and deployment costs. The gains are limited by the eight-person new cohort and unexplained baseline discrepancies between Tables 2 and 5. Broad claims also remain largely unqualified despite 85.2% non-CS success and 100% hinted success on Red Dot. Overall, the added transparency and practical evidence provide a modest quality improvement.
